newsitem.title: DUBAI: Work starts on new 1,300 MW Iran power plant.
newsitem.headline: Work starts on new 1,300 MW Iran power plant.

text.p: Iran has begun construction work on a 1,300 megawatt power plant in the Central Province to meet fast-growing demand for electricity, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported late on Sunday.

At a ground-breaking ceremony in Shazand, 25 km (15 miles) southwest of Arak, Power Organisation of Iran managing director Qasem Mostaqel said the plant would cost about $370 million as well as 102 billion rials ($58.3 million).
Iran normally gives dollar costs for imports and foreign contractors and a rial figure for local costs.
Half the equipment for the plant -- which would provide energy for industry in the region -- would be made by Iranian firms, he said. China would also provide some machinery.
IRNA said Chinese officials were present at the ceremony.

Energy Minister Bijan Namdar Zanganeh said with the commissioning of several new plants up to 2003, 10,000 megawatts would be added to the country's power generation capacity which currently stands at 16,000 megawatts.

Plants under construction included the steam unit of Qom combined cycle power plant, the steam unit of Fars power plant, Shahid Montazeri power station in Isfahan, Karun-3 power plant and Masjid Suleyman power plant.
IRNA did not specify what type of power plant was being constructed at Shazand.
($1=1,750 rials at the official rate for state accounts)
